name: AI Handoff Continuity Benchmark
description: A deterministic benchmark for testing whether a model can recover the state required to continue work from a transcript, compressed memory, or structured handoff.

conditions.label: Conversation transcript
conditions.description: Chronological messages containing relevant state alongside superseded decisions and conversational noise.

conditions.label: Compressed memory
conditions.description: A short free-form summary produced at a checkpoint, with some evidence and rationale omitted.

conditions.label: Structured handoff
conditions.description: An explicit continuation record separating current state, decisions, evidence, constraints, next action, ownership, and open questions.

cases.title: Production cache-header incident
cases.task: Continue the incident response without repeating a failed mitigation or changing production before the remaining validation is complete.

objective.text: Restore correct API caching without causing another production regression.
Increase every API cache TTL to ten minutes.
Replace the CDN before investigating further.

currentState.text: The unsafe global cache rule was rolled back.
A route-scoped header patch is deployed to staging.
The route-scoped patch is already deployed to production.
The incident is closed and needs no further validation.

decisions.text: Apply caching only to the public catalogue route, not authenticated API responses.
Keep the global CDN rule and exempt failures individually.

evidence.text: Trace 1842 shows an authenticated response served with the public cache key.
Staging run 27 shows the catalogue route cached and account routes marked private.
The weekly sales chart increased after the incident.

constraints.text: Production changes require the 14:00 UTC change window and on-call approval.
Do not change the database schema during the incident.
Ship any mitigation immediately without approval.

nextAction.text: Run the authenticated-route header matrix in staging and attach the output for on-call approval.
Reapply the global cache rule in production.
Close the incident without another test.

openQuestions.text: Does the catalogue response still vary by locale after the patch?
When does the CDN vendor contract renew?

contexts.transcript: 09:02 Mina: Customers are seeing another account's stale preferences. Objective is to restore correct API caching without another regression. 09:08 Raj: Trace 1842 has the clue: an authenticated response was served with the public cache key. 09:13 Mina: Let's increase every API cache TTL to ten minutes while we inspect it. 09:24 Raj: I tried a global CDN rule. Error rate rose, so I rolled it back. The unsafe global rule is no longer active. 09:31 Lee: Weekly sales are up; unrelated but adding it here. 09:40 Mina: Decision changed. Cache only the public catalogue route. Authenticated API responses must remain private. Do not change database schema during this incident. 10:05 Raj: Route-scoped patch is in staging. Staging run 27 shows catalogue cached and account routes private. 10:11 Mina: Do not call this fixed yet. Production changes wait for the 14:00 UTC window and on-call approval. 10:16 Raj: One thing is unresolved: locale behavior. Does the catalogue response still vary by locale? 10:20 Mina: I own the next step. Run the authenticated-route header matrix in staging and attach output for my approval.
contexts.memory: Cache incident: a global rule caused problems and was rolled back. A narrower patch is being tested. Mina is coordinating. Production should be handled carefully. There was a trace showing a cache-key issue, but the exact validation and remaining locale question were not retained.
contexts.handoff:
OBJECTIVE
Restore correct API caching without causing another production regression.

CURRENT STATE
- Unsafe global cache rule rolled back.
- Route-scoped header patch deployed to staging; not production.

DECISION
Cache only the public catalogue route. Authenticated API responses remain private.

EVIDENCE
- Trace 1842: authenticated response served with public cache key.
- Staging run 27: catalogue cached; account routes private.

CONSTRAINTS
- Production change only in the 14:00 UTC window with on-call approval.
- No database schema changes during the incident.

NEXT ACTION
Run the authenticated-route header matrix in staging and attach output for approval.

OWNER
Mina, incident commander.

OPEN QUESTION
Does catalogue response still vary by locale?

cases.title: Onboarding drop-off research
cases.task: Continue the analysis using the agreed cohort and avoid presenting an unvalidated explanation as a finding.

objective.text: Identify why eligible new users abandon onboarding before completing business setup.
Maximize app installs regardless of activation.

currentState.text: The event funnel has been verified for the eligible cohort.
Five interview transcripts are collected but not yet coded.
Pricing concern is proven as the primary cause.

decisions.text: Use users eligible for the new onboarding flow after 15 July; exclude employees and test accounts.
Use every install since January, including employees.
Treat pricing concern as the confirmed explanation.

evidence.text: Saved query 6f2 shows 54.1% reach completed intro and 18.9% complete business setup.
Five interview transcripts mention uncertainty around business details, but coding is incomplete.

constraints.text: Do not export names, phone numbers, or transcript PII.
Label qualitative explanations as hypotheses until transcript coding is complete.
Include participant names in the public report.

nextAction.text: Code the five transcripts against the agreed taxonomy and compare themes with funnel stages.
Increase acquisition spend before finishing analysis.

openQuestions.text: Which interview themes correspond to the business-search and verification stages?

contexts.handoff:
OBJECTIVE
Identify why eligible new users abandon onboarding before completing business setup.

CURRENT STATE
- Funnel verified for the agreed eligible cohort.
- Five interview transcripts collected; coding is pending.

DECISION
Cohort is users eligible for the new flow after 15 July, excluding employees and test accounts.

EVIDENCE
- Query 6f2: 54.1% complete intro; 18.9% complete business setup.
- Five transcripts mention uncertainty around business details; this is not yet a coded finding.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not export names, phone numbers, or transcript PII.
- Treat qualitative explanations as hypotheses until coding is complete.

NEXT ACTION
Code five transcripts against the agreed taxonomy and compare themes with funnel stages.

OWNER
Sam, product researcher.

OPEN QUESTION
Which themes correspond to business-search and verification stages?

cases.title: Warehouse refund model revision
cases.task: Continue the SQL model change with the approved grain, filters, and validation before merging.

objective.text: Correct the daily refund model without double-counting partial refunds.

currentState.text: The revised query is drafted on branch refund-grain-v2.
The model is merged and running in production.

decisions.text: Model one row per refund line and aggregate to order-day only in the final CTE.
Keep one row per order throughout the model.
Discard all but the latest refund event.

evidence.text: Fixture refund_edges.csv covers full, partial, repeated, and reversed refunds and currently passes.
The 30-day comparison shows an 82-order difference concentrated in repeated partial refunds.

constraints.text: Do not start the historical backfill until Finance signs off on the comparison.

nextAction.text: Send the 30-day old-vs-new comparison and the 82-order sample to Finance for sign-off.
Merge and start the backfill immediately.
Change reporting boundaries to local time.

openQuestions.text: Will Finance accept the 82-order historical difference as correction rather than variance?
Which chart font should be used?

contexts.handoff:
OBJECTIVE
Correct the daily refund model without double-counting partial refunds.

CURRENT STATE
- Revised query drafted on refund-grain-v2; not merged.
- Six-row refund edge-case fixture passes.

DECISION
Use one row per refund line; aggregate to order-day only in final CTE.

EVIDENCE
- refund_edges.csv covers full, partial, repeated, and reversed refunds; all pass.
- 30-day comparison differs by 82 orders, concentrated in repeated partial refunds.

CONSTRAINTS
- UTC day boundaries.
- Exclude test merchants with dim_merchant.is_test.
- No historical backfill before Finance sign-off.

NEXT ACTION
Send the old-vs-new comparison and 82-order sample to Finance.

OWNER
Priya, analytics engineer.

OPEN QUESTION
Will Finance accept the 82-order difference as a correction rather than variance?
